title.narrative: RECOVER - Reducing Communities’ Vulnerability to Drought and External Shocks (FAO)

description.narrative: (Somalia): With FY 2024 funds, USAID will strengthen leadership and governance structures by establishing committees to address production, performing infrastructure maintenance, undertaking disaster risk mitigation, and building financial literacy capacity. Additionally, Reducing Communities' Vulnerability to Drought and External Shocks (RECOVER) will build capacity in post-harvest techniques such as grain-quality management, improve access to post-harvest equipment such as moisture meters, and invest in grain and cereal storage infrastructure. To improve marketing opportunities, RECOVER will enhance the ability of farmers to aggregate their grain and produce by connecting them with traders while exploring value-addition opportunities. Further, RECOVER will strengthen group governance among cooperatives to increase access to finance through Multinational Finance Institutions..RECOVER is carefully designed to address the interlinked challenges arising from areas prone to climatic hazards and vulnerabilities as well as endemic conflict due to competing land claims, geographical segregation, and moribund local economies, which encourage predation and rent-seeking. In addition to the large-scale infrastructure rehabilitation, the program involves activities that address conflict mitigation, stabilization, and peacebuilding; control flood and soil erosion; strengthen climate-smart production techniques; and increase capacity for effective governance. RECOVER also includes a crisis response mechanism to enable a rapid response when gains achieved by the activity are threatened....

description.narrative: (Somalia): .Nearly 75 percent of Somali women between the ages of 15 and 49 have never attended school. Through support to the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office's successful Adolescent Girls Education in Somalia (AGES) activity, USAID will build the resilience of marginalized households and communities by providing young Somali women basic and financial literacy, numeracy, and soft and life skills. With FY 2022 funds, AGES will increase access to education opportunities for adolescent girls and young women aged 15 to 25 who have never enrolled in or have dropped out of school in Banadir Regional Administration (greater Mogadishu) and Hirshabelle and South West State. Building foundational skills will increase women's participation in productive decisions at the household and community levels. The activity will strengthen young women's networks, support female youth-led advocacy efforts, and foster safe spaces for dialogue. AGES will enhance the economic situation of female youth by forming village savings and loan associations and creating linkages to financial services, social safety nets, and emergency support systems...

description.narrative: (Somalia): .Festering grievances and the government's inability to justly address them create space for al-Shaabab to operate in Somalia. USAID's justice programming enables citizens to navigate formal and customary justice systems and secure rights-based solutions to address their grievances. USAID uses the findings from targeted research to strengthen both formal and customary justice systems to increase their efficiency, legitimacy, and fairness. USAID's program addresses the inequality within formal justice and traditional dispute resolution mechanisms, working to overcome existing divisions along clan, ideological, gender, and political-economic lines. USAID's goal is to safeguard citizen security, expand citizens' access to justice, and create an enabling environment that protects basic human rights. .With FY 2021 resources, USAID programming will improve the capacity and sustainability of civil and justice institutions, strengthen justice sector actors' skills, and enhance coordination among institutions and actors. In parallel, USAID will strengthen legal aid clinics, justice promoter networks, civil society advocates, and academic institutions to enhance the quality of legal services and expand access to justice. USAID will expand programming to target the Banadir region around Mogadishu and other unstable areas of southern Somalia, including South West State. The program will continue to conduct targeted research to examine structural causes of injustice, using the findings to design programming to empower communities and other stakeholders. USAID will explore opportunities to increase good governance by strengthening the capacity of local governance structures to address local-level conflicts that drive instability and foster feelings of injustice.... ..... .

Objectives for Somalia: The Expanding Access to Justice (EAJ) program will strive to increase awareness and general knowledge of legal rights, human rights, and options for recourse, especially for Somali women, youth, and marginalized groups. It will respond to citizens’ needs by supporting civil society and government justice actors in sustainably improving the quality and scope of legal services.The focus is on developing services that assist citizens in achieving rights-based outcomes through both the formal and informal justice system. Working with government and civil society justice sector actors, EAJ’s ultimate goal is to increase the quality, reach, availability, and accessibility of legal aid services of legal aid service delivery in Somalia and Somaliland.

description.narrative: (Somalia): ..Bar Ama Baro (BAB, "Teach or Learn" in Somali), will increase access to quality education for out-of-school children and youth between ages 9-17 in 17 districts spanning Mogadishu, South West State, Hirshabelle, and Jubaland. In partnership with the Federal Government of Somalia (FGS), BAB will increase student enrollment; school safety, literacy, numeracy; and socio-emotional skills acquisition. The program will also support greater government capacity to regulate accelerated basic education. With FY 2022 funds, BAB will revise and distribute learning materials developed for overage learners to complement the government's formal curriculum. Furthermore, USAID will assist the government and the private sector to develop accelerated basic education (ABE) programming and policies on teacher qualifications, instructional time, and academic standards. This latter effort will lead to accreditation of ABE and certification of students so that they may transition into formal schools at the right level. BAB will also foster positive gender norms and reduce educational barriers for girls and boys. In addition, community efforts to support education - from advocacy, mobilization and protection of vulnerable students - will help build resilience to withstand Al-Shabaab's ideological attacks and coercive recruitment techniques. At the same time, BAB is pivoting programming to respond to Somalia's ongoing drought, the country's worst in over 70 years. Specifically, BAB will focus on enabling students to continue to learn during the crisis and will target an additional cohort of learners displaced by the drought. This program complements the planned New Somalia Education Support and Adolescent Girls Education programs (co-funded with the UK)...... ... ........ ..

description.narrative: (Somalia): With FY 2024 resources, USAID, in coordination with the Federal Government of Somalia and in collaboration with the Department of Defense and State Department, will support community-driven stabilization activities that increase the legitimacy of local authorities and support them to manage conflict and prevent a resurgence of violence. USAID will help establish the conditions to build local institutions that are inclusive, responsive, and accountable to all groups, including minority and marginalized populations. USAID will continue to prioritize areas recently recovered from al-Shabaab. Furthermore, USAID's stabilization programs will continue to support community-prioritized development activities to demonstrate the positive impact of political reconciliation and assist in rebuilding relationships between the government and local communities. USAID will create platforms and mechanisms that bring communities together to identify sources of conflict and conduct activities that address grievances and rebuild trust between conflicting groups. .In addition, USAID, with FY 2024 resources, will work to increase the participation of youth and other marginalized groups in local governance. Leveraging women's role as peace builders and mediators in times of conflict, USAID will seek to increase women's participation in newly constituted governance structures in recently stabilized communities. In particular, Gender Equity and Equality Action Fund Priority 5 will expand women's access to political, economic, and social opportunities and strengthen their capacity to be active decision-makers in political and economic arenas. ....

description.narrative: (Somalia): With FY 2024 funds, USAID will promote livelihood and income diversification, increase social and economic connections, facilitate access to finance in rural and urban areas at the community and at the broader systemic level, by influencing policies that impact the community as a whole. For communities involved in the livestock sector, USAID will support a private sector to adopt drought-tolerant fodder varieties. USAID will expand rural, climate-smart investment opportunities and strengthen associations and cooperatives in priority sectors..To advance livelihood diversification and adaptation, USAID will target the fisheries sector in several coastal communities. To build social and economic connections and access to finance for marginalized communities, USAID will increase the capacity and accessibility of economic associations, such as fisheries cooperatives, Village Savings and Loans Associations, self-help groups, and agricultural industry associations. In addition, IRiS will focus on enhancing the Somali Seafood Export Association, a platform connecting export market actors. This will involve providing strategic technical assistance, developing governance structures, and expanding the association's membership base. IRiS aligns to Gender Equity and Equality Action Fund Priorities 3 and 5. Under priority 3, IRiS will support women's economic future by helping smallholder women farmers build resilience to climate change by adopting climate-smart livelihoods. Under priority 5, IRiS will expand women's access to political and social opportunities and strengthen their active decision-making capacity. Through its Gender Inclusion and Disability Action Plan, IRiS promotes equal access to all economic opportunities.. Availability of nutritious foods, will indirectly improve nutrition. .IRiS attributes $1,500,000 to Adaptation-Indirect and will promote livelihood and income diversification towards more resilient and climate-smart livelihoods. ...

description.narrative: (Somalia): While Al-Shabaab serves as a credible alternative to the state in much of southern Somalia, it has not been able to transcend clan politics and struggles to provide inclusive or responsive governance. The 2022 uprisings in Hirshabelle are an example of al-Shabaab's failures to overcome these issues. Layering over prior stabilization efforts, USAID will strengthen legitimate and effective local governance as part of its efforts to offer an alternative to al-Shabaab rule in southern Somalia. Working in partnership with local, state, and federal governments, this program recognizes that efforts to consolidate prior stabilization gains will require a mixture of reconciliation and local governance programming. This program is designed to sequence and layer over other USAID/donor-funded inter-communal reconciliation and stabilization activities..With FY 2024 resources, USAID will support local governments to better manage resources and identify and respond to citizen priorities, improving the performance and quality of local governance in Somalia. Specifically, USAID will provide capacity building to established or emerging governance structures to deliver tangible improvements and promote participatory processes that seek citizen input to identify key needs and priorities. With FY 2024 resources, USAID will focus on providing a voice to youth, women, minorities, and marginalized groups to positively engage in, and contribute to, political processes. In particular, USAID will identify and support civil society and community-based organizations to represent and advocate citizen interests while holding the government to account. Recognizing that enabling communities to plan for future shocks and climate risks is key to effective governance, USAID will, whenever possible, work with local governance structures to strengthen their disaster risk-reduction efforts and contribute to Adaptation-Indirect....... .

description.narrative: (Somalia): Basic education is the foundation for increased access to economic, social, and political opportunities and broader resilience to withstand al-Shabaab's ideological attacks and coercive recruitment techniques. The Accelerated Education Activity will provide accelerated basic education and non-formal education for out-of-school children and youth between the ages of 12 to 25. The activity will target 17 districts, prioritizing marginalized areas of south and central Somalia. This activity has four expected results: 1) increase equitable access to accelerated basic education and non-formal education programs; 2) improve learning outcomes in foundational skills areas (such as literacy, numeracy, and social-emotional learning); 3) increase community engagement and local ownership of accelerated and non-formal education programming; and 4) strengthen the capacity of government at local and federal levels to oversee the provision of quality public education..With FY 2024 funds, the activity will revise and distribute learning materials developed for accelerated basic education and non-formal learners to complement the government's formal curriculum. USAID will partner with federal- and state-level education ministries to provide in-service training for teachers and assist the government and the private sector to develop programming and policies on teacher qualifications, instructional time, and academic standards. This latter effort will lead to accreditation and certification of students so that they may transition into formal schools at the right level. To promote inclusion, the activity will foster positive gender norms, implement safe learning environment standards, and reduce educational barriers for girls and boys. This activity will also be "shock responsive," able to pivot programming to provide critical education support in the event that target populations are displaced by droughts, floods, or conflict..... .. .....

description.narrative: The TRANSFORM project aims to improve food security and resilience in Somalia by rehabilitating critical infrastructure and promoting climate smart agriculture for smallholder farmers in Jowhar. The project will support Somali farmers with flood protection and reliable irrigation, helping them to use their land more productively and sustainably. This effort includes developing a comprehensive JOSP governance plan, conducting environmental and social safeguarding studies, as well as addressing conflict mitigation, land tenure management, and durable solutions for displaced populations.

description.narrative: The Somali Interactive Radio Instruction Program (SIRIP) advances stabilization in Somalia by delivering education in a precarious situation and by giving children the capabilities they will need to actively participate in society. SIRIP, funded by the United States Agency for International Development and implemented by Education Development Center, provides high quality interactive audio programs to Somali children attending formal, non-governmental, and Quranic schools, as well as non-formal community learning centers. With the assistance of audio programs, teachers lead classes and are trained in using interactive teaching methods including stories, activities, and educational songs. Supplemental materials accompany the programs, providing schools with the resources to support sound, primary-level instruction.

title.narrative: Bringing Unity, Integrity, and Legitimacy to Democracy (BUILD) in Somalia

description.narrative: (Somalia): .Although Somalia is moving towards more inclusive institutions and systems, there is a long way to go to ensure the political inclusion of all Somalis, particularly youth, women, and marginalized clans. In late 2020 or early 2021, Somalia is scheduled to hold its first planned one person, one vote elections in more than fifty years. .USAID promotes political inclusion by strengthening electoral and political processes across Somalia and supporting joint international donor efforts for planned upcoming elections. USAID also builds civil society organizations' capacity to engage citizens and monitor elections and political processes, strengthens the capacity of election management bodies to administer credible elections, and supports the development of viable, issue-based political parties. As elections approach, USAID will focus on enabling a credible and more inclusive process that is accepted by Somalis and enhances Somalia's stability. .With FY 2019 resources, USAID will increase its focus on political parties in response to closing political space. Credible political parties offer the best hope of moving Somalia beyond clan-based politics. USAID will continue to focus on increasing women, youth, and other marginalized groups' participation in the political process by promoting increased civic engagement and strengthening the capacity of civil society organizations and the media to advocate for their greater political inclusion. To strengthen the enabling environment for political inclusion, USAID will support the development and adoptions of laws, regulations, policies, and best practices. This will ensure that each stage of the electoral cycle enables greater inclusion on the one hand, while strengthening the capacity of key institutions to administer the process on the other. ...

title.narrative: Harnessing Opportunities for Peaceful Engagement in Afgoye (HOPE)

description.narrative: The Harnessing Opportunities for Peaceful Engagement in Afgoye (HOPE) project is designed to increase community resilience to violence in Afgoye District of Lower Shebelle Region in South West Federal Administration of Somalia by strengthening community relations and decision-making at the local level. It employs a people-to-people approach, aiming to create change at both the attitudinal and institutional levels, a combination which is critical for effectiveness and long-term impact. Two objectives guide our people-to-people approach: First, the project will foster constructive interaction at the community level to improve understanding of key issues, strengthen relationships and enable collective action to address shared concerns. Second, it will strengthen the local government to perform their roles effectively, improve decision-making and establish linkages with their constituents. The HOPE project will foster positive relationships at two levels: among communities and between communities and local government.

title.narrative: Somalis Harmonizing Inter- and Intra-Communal Relationships (SHIIR)

description.narrative: (Somalia): USAID will support activities that involve capacity building.in key governance institutions by providing capacity building for local.government in high-risk areas of Somalia. .To deepen.the understanding of how citizens and government can effectively work.together, SHIIR and their local partners will deliver civic awareness.education programs to citizens, clan elders and district administrators in four.targeted areas in Somalia. Using the Wadajir framework (National Framework.for Local Governance) as the basis for discussions of good governance and.accountability, SHIIR will help government and citizens to better understand.their roles in their local government . .After the.trainings, SHIIR will bring together community members and local.government for civic dialogues, giving district administrators' practical.experience in how to engage their citizenry, in consultations encourage public.participation and act as accountable stewards of public resources.

description.narrative: (Somalia): USAID will support community-driven stabilization activities to create conditions where locally legitimate authorities can peaceably manage conflict and prevent a resurgence of violence. USAID activities will set the conditions for building legitimate societal and governing institutions that are inclusive, responsive, and accountable to all groups, including minority and marginalized populations. The intent is to lay the foundation for legitimate political stability that is required for longer term development efforts to take root..With FY 2019 resources, USAID's stabilization program will add a rapid response mechanism to support early recovery in newly cleared areas. USAID will also conduct contextual analysis to inform current and planned stabilization operations and use the research to conduct partner preparatory dialogues prior to entry in these newly recovered areas. .USAID's stabilization program will continue to support reconstruction and development activities to demonstrate the positive impact of the political reconciliation process and assist in strengthening relationships between the government and local communities. Representatives from target communities will come together to prioritize and select community activities to be implemented. USAID will also support communities to transition from stabilization to longer term development as appropriate. In areas where community consensus planning and physical construction have been completed, local governance bodies, in conjunction with civil society actors, will oversee operations and maintenance. USAID will also implement local reconciliation activities to increase dialogue on peace and recovery..Youth and marginalized groups can become potential "destabilizers" if their voice is unheard. This program will also focus on increasing their voices in governance, working to increase the participation of youth and marginalized groups in local governance. ....

description.narrative: Under the Monitoring and Evaluation Program for Somalia (MEPS), IBTCI is leading a range of M&E and technical assistance activities on behalf of USAID/East Africa and DfID. IBTCI provides regular, hands-on technical assistance to USAID and Implementing Partners in the development of PMPs and M&E Plans, and has provided cross-sector technical guidance on the identification, development and measurement of stabilization and sector-specific indicators for several PMPs. IBTCI is carrying out 1st, 2nd and 3rd tier verifications throughout all regions of Somalia, with its network of local Third-Party Monitors (TPMs).Under MEPS, IBTCI has led evaluations of programs focusing on youth livelihoods and small grants/transition initiatives, as well as a broad assessment of international donor activities throughout Somalia which provided recommendations and findings to inform the Mission's reformulation of its strategy through 2014. IBTCI has also overseen and provided technical assistance to several surveys, facilitated and led several retreats and training sessions, and promoted collaboration among various donors and local government entities.

description.narrative: (Somalia): To continue strengthening the Government of Somalia's ability to deliver sound governance and oversee the delivery of key services to its citizens, USAID will strengthen public financial management systems, domestic revenue mobilization, expenditure control, and accountability in the Federal Government of Somalia and Federal Member States. USAID will focus on building the capacity of resource management systems, the intergovernmental fiscal framework, and support the delivery of key services including health and education. At the same time, USAID will enhance accountability around the delivery of those key services. This activity is implemented through a Public International Organization Agreement with the World Bank..

description.narrative: Improve the ability of the USG, host countries and other partners to prepare for and mitigate the effects of disasters, including both natural disasters and complex emergencies, taking into account the differences in men and womens freedom of movement and access to information. Activities under this component include any efforts to enhance the capacities of the USG (in Washington and in the field), humanitarian assistance providers, national host-country authorities, and local communities to engage in disaster reduction and response activities. Activities consist of standardized and coordinated assessments, monitoring, information sharing, data and situational analysis, joint planning; enhancement of coping mechanisms, including the capacity to address adaptation to constantly changing situations on the ground including climate variability and climate change.

description.narrative: Improve the ability of the USG, host countries and other partners to prepare for and mitigate the effects of disasters, including both natural disasters and complex emergencies, taking into account the differences in men and womens freedom of movement and access to information. Activities under this component include any efforts to enhance the capacities of the USG (in Washington and in the field), humanitarian assistance providers, national host-country authorities, and local communities to engage in disaster reduction and response activities. Activities consist of standardized and coordinated assessments, monitoring, information sharing, data and situational analysis, joint planning; enhancement of coping mechanisms, including the capacity to address adaptation to constantly changing situations on the ground including climate variability and climate change.

description.narrative: Improve the ability of the USG, host countries and other partners to prepare for and mitigate the effects of disasters, including both natural disasters and complex emergencies, taking into account the differences in men and womens freedom of movement and access to information. Activities under this component include any efforts to enhance the capacities of the USG (in Washington and in the field), humanitarian assistance providers, national host-country authorities, and local communities to engage in disaster reduction and response activities. Activities consist of standardized and coordinated assessments, monitoring, information sharing, data and situational analysis, joint planning; enhancement of coping mechanisms, including the capacity to address adaptation to constantly changing situations on the ground including climate variability and climate change.

description.narrative: Reduce the threat or impact of violent conflict and promote the peaceful resolution of differences, mitigate violence if it has already broken out, or establish a framework for peace and reconciliation. This is done by identifying the causes of conflict and state failure; supporting early responses that address the causes and consequences of instability and conflict; and developing long lasting solutions to the problems that drive conflict. This includes support for processes and mechanisms for reconciliation and conflict mitigation no matter what the source of the conflict may be, though this may require integration with other elements.

This sub-element may also include developing and disseminating best practices and lessons learned, testing demonstration and/or pilot models, or the preparation of strategic plans and other short-term programming tasks.
